analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the Lee Resolution introduced June 7 1776, its three parts, the three committees appointed June 11 1776, the July 2 adoption, the July 9 1776 New York vote, and treaty and confederation delays until September 1776 and November 1777

overview.headline: Lee Resolution proposed independence and led to committees for declaration and alliances in 1776

keyPoints.point: Richard Henry Lee introduced a resolution proposing independence in the Second Continental Congress on June 7 1776
keyPoints.quote: On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution in the Second Continental Congress proposing independence for the American colonies.

keyPoints.point: The Lee Resolution contained three parts including a declaration of independence and a plan for confederation
keyPoints.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

keyPoints.point: Congress appointed three concurrent committees to draft the declaration and to prepare alliance and confederation plans
keyPoints.quote: On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution

keyPoints.point: Approval was deferred until July 2 while members obtained instructions and Congress adopted the declaration portion
keyPoints.quote: approval was deferred until July 2. On that date, Congress adopted the first part (the declaration).

keyTerms.gloss: delegates gathering that became the governing body of the union during the Revolution
keyTerms.quote: The colonists elected delegates to attend a Continental Congress that eventually became the governing body of the union during the Revolution.

keyTerms.gloss: authorizing body in Virginia that gave instruction to propose independence
keyTerms.quote: acting under the instruction of the Virginia Convention.

keyTerms.gloss: resolution with declaration and alliance and confederation elements
keyTerms.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

keyTerms.gloss: planned partnerships forming support from other nations
keyTerms.quote: a second to draw up a plan "for forming foreign alliances," and a third to "prepare and digest the form of a confederation."

keyTerms.gloss: plan for uniting colonies under a shared structure delayed until later approval
keyTerms.quote: The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776; the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.
